approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It draws breeding sources across high-scoring quantiles, makes connected-fragment crossover products or short walks of weighted atom and bond edits, and greedily keeps 64 survivors. It stores every accepted observation in a task-local archive. Before each announced batch it fits a Gaussian process on chirality-aware Morgan environment counts, generates a fresh pool of 160 novel graphs, and chooses evaluations with correlated posterior samples. Stable isomeric identities and a narrow sulfur rule check final products against the original scored generating parents. The aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange route has already been removed; occasional second and third mutation calls remain.
approach.novelty: Replace the neighborhood explored by one mutation call with a randomized molecular serialization followed by exactly one SELFIES token insertion, deletion or replacement. Branch and ring tokens can expose different connected alternatives under the same requested call schedule. This keeps the useful original crossover construction and continuation law. Siblings instead restricted crossover with BRICS typing, increased continuation frequency, or changed learned allocation; none tested this fixed grammar neighborhood. Its value depends on stronger accepted alternatives and their later use, rather than string diversity or valence validity alone.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior on actual code Parent n-1744a1494180 is limited productive alternatives around successful local molecular families. Its full published molecular assessment reports repeated halogen/short-chain/sulfur/carbonyl variations and inconsistent preservation of useful functional-group context, with reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unassigned stereochemistry. Distinct compact families across seeds are contrary evidence to a claim of global scaffold collapse. I read all three actual summary.json/run.log pairs: all are complete, with mean final Top-1 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. A new read-only reconstruction from all fifteen actual accepted-observation logs finds 648 strict original-best-parent beats out of 4350 offspring, mean offspring score 0.37204956084218205 against mean best generating-parent score 0.45530404483359543, positive parent-margin mass 17.25153528627184, and 255 sequential incumbent gains totaling 5.819415048695714. This does not identify the seven-primitive mutation menu as the cause. Current-Parent typed construction n-55d120396e72 loses 0.09479254157802065 despite real useful cores and descendants; heavier ordinary continuation n-9d88f032c4dc loses 0.038954730839330654 despite 390 affected evaluated finals and 73 later breeders. Conversely continuation removal n-c070e95b09ef loses 0.03069975142490533 and original crossover removal n-6059424cc614 loses 0.043639786851491315, supporting preservation of those existing routes under their own conditions. The new question changes reachable neighbors per call while holding those consumers and requested effort fixed. All fifteen endpoints, including the Parent late deco_hop seed-zero breakthrough at evaluation 281, remain in the primary comparison.

literature_review.conclusion: This is a new searched review, not a claimed reused recorded-node review. I read the supplied private primary review .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r32-search-policy/external-method-review.md, then performed the two queries above, read the primary papers through the recorded channels and downloaded/hash-checked the pinned official implementations under .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r32-slot1-plan/. Official examples' nonisomeric/unbounded/library-comparison behavior is outside the experiment. Source/release inspection and read-only Parent reconstruction establish a reviewable intervention, not a new oracle score, efficacy, chemical mediation or independent realization. Adequate natural product/accepted/descendant exposure and the complete matched +0.002 endpoint criterion must answer it; one complete exposed negative answer ends this fixed recipe.

hypothesis: Replace only the shared bounded GraphOperators.mutate neighborhood with a STONED-inspired randomized-serialization single-token SELFIES operation: one fresh session-RNG atom permutation of the current input graph, identity-preserving isomeric Kekule SMILES, strict SELFIES 2.2.0 encoding under its default semantic constraints, then a uniform insertion/deletion/replacement at a uniform eligible token position, using the complete sorted default semantic robust alphabet and excluding same-token replacement. Decode the edited string exactly once and use the exact inherited checked_molecule/max_atoms result. Representation failures and invalid/empty/oversize products spend one of the existing twelve internal attempts; valid graph no-ops remain valid returns and final novelty/admission decides them. All ordinary requested calls, higher-floor escalation, optional crossover finishing, original crossover construction, scored-parent references, sulfur/identity gates, archive/survival and count-GP allocation remain intact. The hypothesized path is changed graph reachability to larger absolute useful accepted gains and productive core descendants, potentially raising the complete endpoint mean.

finding_summary.headline: SELFIES edits reached scored descendants but reduced useful gains and the complete endpoint mean
finding_summary.insights: Broader graph reachability and real breeding reuse did not produce stronger useful alternatives in this setting. A single token could remove more than one hundred atoms; ordinary-call Morgan similarity fell from 0.703 to 0.472. The original predictor remained prospective and mathematically unchanged, and its MSE on accepted labels and within-batch ordering improved while absolute molecular utility fell. Correct construction and predictor fidelity are established; the adverse contrast therefore concerns the new neighborhood and its ensuing adaptive history. The Molecular assessment suggests disrupted functional-group relationships, large repeated assemblies and electronically incomplete charged or radical-bearing output as plausible explanations. Conventional high scoring families also survive, so these chemistry observations do not identify a single cause or justify a blanket chemical rule. More cores and descendants are insufficient evidence of productive exploration. The fixed recipe now has a complete exposed negative answer; the separate effects of serialization, token operations and ensuing chemistry remain unresolved, and no transfer or tuning result follows.
finding_summary.results: The grammar executed and delivered changed molecules through both ordinary mutation and crossover finishing: 2,888 accepted offspring contained a successful SELFIES call, and 2,866 had an effective graph change. All 15 sessions completed their 300 observations, and every admitted pool and final suggestion remained compliant. New typed cores rose from 1,820 to 2,422, but strict wins over the original scored parents fell from 648 to 487. The sum of positive parent margins fell from 17.251535 to 10.324590, and total sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.819415 to 3.906773. Productive new typed cores had a larger unique accepted-descendant union, yet those descendants added less incumbent gain: 3.438632 versus 4.900088. The complete endpoint mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.468944, a paired loss of 0.127509. All three seed macros and 13 of 15 task endpoints declined, contradicting the required +0.002 gain. The two improving endpoints remain in the result.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl families coexist with naked ions, radical-bearing graphs, cumulenes and oversized ester/peroxide assemblies
molecular.overall_character: Node n-700f8a4cd559 produces azaaryl amides and ketenimines, aryl-linked open-chain and cyclic amines, piperazine/pyrimidinedione combinations, fluorinated phenolic nitrogen/carbonyl series, and large linked heterocycle/ester/peroxide assemblies. All 15 Child and 15 published code-Parent n-1744a1494180 search trajectory files were read completely: each session contains 300 observations, including 10 initials and 290 accepted optimizer observations. Both nodes therefore have 900 records and 870 optimizer observations per objective. No path, task or paired seed comparison is missing. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile-mismatched seeds; the supplied Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile uses batch size 10. Published Parent trajectories, including its late seed-0 evaluation-281 heterocycle breakthrough, remain the comparison authority. The digest final-molecule excerpts are recent proposals, not the best molecules of all seeds. Digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.8621 to 0.9598, aromatic-string incidence from 0.5598 to 0.9356, and charged-string incidence from 0.2828 to 0.8195. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 descriptions of the 4350 Child optimizer observations find rings in 4050 and aromatic atoms in 3613. Charged atoms occur in 2340 observations, and RDKit assigns nonzero radical electrons to 1679; the corresponding Parent counts are both zero. Boron and phosphorus occur in 875 and 830 Child observations, respectively, versus zero for each in Parent. These overlapping observation counts do not measure isolability, electronic ground states or synthetic routes. Bare bracketed carbon/boron centres, multiply negative fluorocarbon fragments, peroxides and reactive unsaturation occur repeatedly among high-label molecules. Their prevalence supports the overall implausible synthetic reading and weak medicinal-chemistry reading, while ordinary neutral azaaryl amides and the best piperazine/dione family provide plausible counterexamples. Raw size, connectivity and elemental variation is broad; within-seed leaders often remain close relatives, and broader raw graph coverage supplies no demonstrated breadth of feasible high-label alternatives. The narrow inherited sulfur condition supplies no whole-molecule chemical certificate. All quoted Child SMILES are in the digest or trusted Child search trajectories; Parent chemistry is described from its published paths and full indexed assessment. Atom/ring/motif descriptions and path hashes are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/L01-resume-20261003/r32-slot1-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_receipt.json. Indexed n-c55c3d520a2c, n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180 reports preserve the original sources of recurring gaps. Score gradients below are associations in accepted labeled molecules, with no target-pharmacophore inference, component attribution or labels assigned to rejected, intermediate or unselected products. The gaps describe conditional future capabilities and do not extend the registered fixed-neighborhood experiment.

per_task.generated_character: Median Child size is 24 heavy atoms, matching Parent; Child proposals range from 1 to 44. The seed-0 leader is a 25-heavy-atom, three-ring N-methylindole/anilide framework with an undercoordinated carbon cation and an N-anionic methoxy attachment. The seed-1 leader has 24 heavy atoms and two rings, including an aromatic-labelled eight-membered diaza ring, an aldehyde, methoxy and formally cationic N/C centres. Seed 2 instead reaches a neutral 23-heavy-atom molecule with two pyridyl rings, a ketone, ethoxy/methyl substitution and a terminal ketenimine segment C=C=N. A neutral methoxy/N-methylindole aryl amide is also present and looks much more accessible by ordinary synthesis. The digest reports ring and aromatic text incidences 0.9379 and 0.8241; charged and cumulated-double-bond text incidences are 0.5782 and 0.3034. Ring chemistry is abundant, but electronic and functional-group quality varies sharply.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader is net neutral yet contains two charged atoms and a perceived radical electron. Net charge alone misses its electronic incompleteness.
The seed-1 leader has net charge +2 and two perceived radical electrons, plus unverified geometry of an aromatic-labelled eight-membered ring.

Ketenimines and carbon-centred cumulated double bonds require environment-specific stability assessment; 259 of 870 Child observations have a perceived carbon centre bearing two double bonds, versus 1 in Parent.

Independent conventional alternatives retaining the useful functional relationships are less evident among leaders than repeated charged or cumulene-bearing relatives; the record supplies no exact missing target scaffold.

In Child seed 0, redistributing fluorinated carbon-anion/N-F attachments across similar aryl/urea/enamine frameworks gives labels 0.6637461664353687 at evaluation 186 and 0.6637461664353685 at evaluations 221 and 265. A relative with net charge -5 and seven perceived radical electrons still scores 0.6607047791245215 at evaluation 212. Replacing one urea-like N-substituted carbonyl region by a hydroxy-carbon substituent in the final seed-0 molecule yields 0.0010332309763978263. The 51-heavy-atom elaborate seed-2 proposal at evaluation 38 scores 5.322365956559792e-37; B#C and final seed-2 methane are also near zero. Labels associate with a particular compact polar/aryl/carbonyl arrangement and tolerate pronounced electronic pathology. They do not establish that naked anions, N-F or boron are chemically necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Newly documented in source n-700f8a4cd559 versus code Parent n-1744a1494180 under Research-in-Depth epoch 1, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch 10 and 300 observations per independent session. Of 4350 Child optimizer observations, 2340 contain charged atoms and RDKit 2023.09.6 assigns nonzero radical electrons to 1679; both Parent counts are zero. Bare carbon/boron centres and multiply negative fluorocarbon chains occur among leaders. One 28-heavy-atom leader has net charge -4 and six perceived radical electrons. Neutral closed-shell aryl amides, aryl/polyamines and piperazine/diones are observed counterexamples, so this is a consistency gap rather than inability to emit ordinary chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently construct complete electronic states and coordinated local environments when introducing charge or new elements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A future task-agnostic generator needs transformations that express complete hydrogen, valence, charge and coordination environments while retaining useful relationships learned from its own accepted feedback. Conventional ions and well-formed organoboron or organophosphorus chemistry should remain expressible. Token representability and net neutrality alone do not establish electronic completeness; this output association does not identify a component or authorize an alphabet or chemistry-gate sweep.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The context-preservation gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c, is carried through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, and is re-observed in n-700f8a4cd559 under the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per session. Child emits 171 observations with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 82, including an isolated H radical. Tiny fragments often receive floor labels. Other seeds expand to 120 heavy atoms; one low-label seed has median size 81 and an amide/sulfonamide leader, whereas high-label families retain available aryl-associated aliphatic amines. A 27-heavy-atom neutral piperazine/dione relative retains a strong label, so useful simplification is already possible. A local urea-like carbonyl alteration in another compact series sharply loses its label despite retaining much of the scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful functional-group relationships are inconsistently preserved through fragmentation, expansion and local substitution.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately rebuild intact functional groups and their relative placement using current-session accepted feedback. Distinguish available amines from amide/sulfonamide-bound nitrogens and meaningful simplification from loss of chemical context. Permit useful growth and shrinking; no universal size threshold, particular ring scaffold or component-specific cause follows from these conditional observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The local-environment concern was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and retained with narrow sulfur conditions in n-1744a1494180. Source n-700f8a4cd559 re-observes it on the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per session. Child has 481 peroxide-containing optimizer observations versus Parent 127, and a 120-heavy-atom leader carries repeated peroxide/ester linkers. N-F, N-O, N-S, ketenimine and enamine environments occur among leaders. Child N-halogen incidence falls to 257 observations from Parent 786 and sulfur-halogen incidence to 3 from 93; these reductions coexist with new electronic liabilities and do not establish overall chemical improvement. Neutral aryl amides and ordinary piperazine/diones remain positive counterexamples to universal dependence on reactive attachments.
transferable_gaps.gap: Representable local bonds still include reactive peripheral environments around otherwise recognizable molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate conventional environment-preserving alternatives around learned aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships, with local treatment of reactive linkers and heteroatom attachments. Recognizable useful groups can coexist with particular liabilities, and permitted sulfur states supply only their original narrow condition. A broad group ban or new filter has no demonstrated score benefit in this evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and persists through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. Source n-700f8a4cd559 re-observes it under the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per session. Child has 154 optimizer observations with ring triple bonds versus Parent 13, and 591 with a carbon centre bearing two double bonds versus Parent 12. Leaders include a five-membered cyclic cumulene, aromatic-labelled eight/nine-membered nitrogen rings and medium-ring closures. Small unsaturated-ring observation count decreases from Parent 402 to Child 214, showing that the liability changes form. The strongest conventional piperazine/dione family instead uses ordinary six-membered rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich graph output does not consistently provide credible geometry for unusual unsaturation and connected-ring topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A future generator needs sensitivity to ring size, unsaturation, coordination and bridge connectivity when constructing alternative molecular arrangements. Offer feasible saturated or differently connected alternatives where meaningful. Ring digits and aromatic labels alone supply no conformational evidence, and neither all small rings nor all fused, medium or large rings warrant exclusion.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The unspecified-stereochemistry gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is carried through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. It is re-observed in n-700f8a4cd559 under the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per session. Every digest stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, and no Child optimizer SMILES has tetrahedral or slash/backslash stereochemical marks. RDKit 2023.09.6 perceives unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2553 of 4350 Child observations versus Parent 2455, including the strongest substituted piperazine molecule. Some leaders have no perceived tetrahedral centre, and formally perceived centres in unstable graphs do not establish isolable stereoisomers.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic arrangements and geometrically distinct unsaturated forms remain unspecified after generation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve configurational identity where chemically meaningful, including relevant alkene/cumulene geometry, while handling achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Protonation, tautomerism and electronic completeness are separate questions. These observations establish neither a universal stereochemical score penalty nor attribution to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading-family gap was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, and remains conditional evidence in n-700f8a4cd559 under the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per session. Different seeds now reach genuinely different ring and linker arrangements, yet leading excerpts repeatedly vary charged side chains, fluorinated attachments, boron substitution, or short peripheral groups on retained aryl/carbonyl/amine relationships. Several rearrangements of an electronically implausible compact family have essentially identical labels. Ordinary neutral aryl amides and a conventional piperazine/dione family provide feasible counterexamples; the evidence supports incomplete useful coverage, not global scaffold collapse.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad raw graph variation does not consistently yield independent feasible alternatives to a successful local molecular family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Construct chemically independent, feasible connectivities retaining relationships supported by the generator's own current-session observations. Assess labeled utility and molecular plausibility separately. Distinct strings, extra elements or large ring-count variation do not establish useful alternatives or a guaranteed benefit from more diversity; this capability requires separate future registration from the completed fixed recipe.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
